Build the structural matrix T of the LDL parametrization

Source: R/dag_layer.R
mc_build_T_matrix.Rd

Assembles the unit lower-triangular matrix \(T\) of the modified Cholesky (LDL) parametrization of a directed acyclic graph (DAG) on \(R\) responses, in which the between-response covariance is \(\Sigma_b = T^{-1} D (T^{-1})^\top\) with \(D\) diagonal and positive (Pourahmadi, 1999). Each edge \(i \to j\) contributes one structural coefficient \(\gamma_{ji}\), the regression coefficient of response \(j\) on its parent \(i\), and the responses are listed in a topological order of the graph (parents before children).

Usage

mc_build_T_matrix(gamma, R, edges = NULL)

Arguments

gamma

finite numeric vector of structural coefficients, exactly one per edge.

R

a single positive integer, the number of responses.

edges

optional integer matrix with columns \((i, j)\), \(i < j\), the directed edges \(i \to j\). If NULL, the complete DAG on the natural ordering \(1 < 2 < \dots < R\) is used. Each edge must occur exactly once; duplicated rows, including reversed duplicates, are rejected because they do not define distinct structural coordinates. A row given as \((j, i)\) with \(j > i\) is read as the same edge \(i \to j\): the direction always follows the natural order of the responses. The rows are sorted lexicographically before use, and gamma is read in that sorted order, not in the order the rows were supplied. Sort the matrix yourself, or read the order back from the edges component of the result, whenever the correspondence matters.

Value

The \(R \times R\) unit lower-triangular matrix \(T\) with \(T_{ji} = -\gamma_{ji}\) for each edge \(i \to j\) and zero elsewhere off the diagonal. Its determinant is one.

References

Pourahmadi, M. (1999). Joint mean-covariance models with applications to longitudinal data: unconstrained parameterisation. Biometrika 86(3), 677-690. doi:10.1093/biomet/86.3.677

See also

mc_build_D_matrix, mc_cholesky_to_covariance

Other directed layer: mc_build_D_matrix(), mc_cholesky_derivatives(), mc_cholesky_to_covariance(), mc_cholesky_to_precision(), mc_dag_closed_root(), mc_dag_coefficients(), mc_dag_sensitivity(), mc_dag_unit_diagonal()

Examples

mc_build_T_matrix(c(0.4, 0.2, 0.3), R = 3)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]  1.0  0.0    0
#> [2,] -0.4  1.0    0
#> [3,] -0.2 -0.3    1
